        (fnn-with-roster (service)
          (setf (fnn-owner-service-publisher service) nil
                (fnn-owner-service-workers service)

    (when pin (fnn-arena-unpin pin))
    (fnn-owner-service-nursery))
  ...
  (fnn-owner-maybe-publish service))
fnn-owner-maybe-publish (5171-5179) does statvfs, runs a gated quantum that can fnn-log-rotate, runs fnn-log-prepare-spare (creates, preallocates and fences a file in staging/), and re-raises fault and indeterminate with `(error e)`. fnn-owner-wait-workers (4804-4811) is documented as 'Join client workers before closing any shared journal or Store object'.
fix: Keep the thread in the roster until it truly finishes: do the follow-up publish decision before the roster removal, inside the same handler. Or post the re-decision to the accept loop with a flag instead of running it on the departing thread, and move the unpin before deregistration.
notes: 10-02 22:32 coded on lane/host-lifecycle 4e409a9d6 (handed to runner); see lanedumps/host-lifecycle.md for verification
reviewer: owner.lisp:5147-5162: the publisher removes itself from workers and then still runs fnn-arena-unpin, the nursery and fnn-owner-maybe-publish. maybe-publish (5171-5179) does statvfs, a gated quantum and, on :needs-spare, fnn-log-prepare-spare (staging I/O). fnn-owner-wait-workers (4804-4811) therefore no longer waits for this work. The new-publisher half is mostly refuted: the quantum checks STOPPING (5212-5214), and a publisher it creates is pushed into workers under the same roster lock. The prepare-spare race with store close and the late unpin are still real. maybe-publish re-raises fault and indeterminate (5176) with no handler on this thread. The image is built with --disable-debugger (build.lisp:622), so that kills the process with exit 1, skipping the fence and settlement, even without a SIGTERM.
scenario: SIGTERM arrives while a publication finishes. The publisher deregisters, so fnn-owner-wait-workers sees an empty roster and cleanup goes on to fnn-owner-store-settlement and closes the Store. Meanwhile the thread, now invisible to cleanup, is inside fnn-log-prepare-spare writing into the store's staging/ directory, or racing the gate. If its first quantum ran before STOPPING was set, it can also push a new publisher into workers after wait-workers returned, which turns a clean exit into 'workers remain' and an uncertain exit. Any error it raises (re-raised at 5176, or a gate failure) is unhandled in a non-main thread. Under --disable-debugger that exits the process with code 1, skipping the fence and settlement. fnn-owner-export-captured (5408-5415) likewise unpins the arena after deregistering.
title: The publisher thread removes itself from the joined worker roster, then keeps doing store I/O and may start another publisher
